target: page 1:3 — 55 boards carrying a status marker
claim: The file marks boards the code cannot produce in FOUR different spellings: '[design-ahead] X' (23), '[not-implemented] X' (9), 'X — UNBUILDABLE — reason' (7), 'X — RETIRED <date> (reason)' (16).
truth: Three distinct claims are hiding in four spellings. 'The code has no producer but it could be built' and 'the product cannot produce this state by construction' are genuinely different, and both differ from 'superseded by another board'. The current set mixes them: 'Layers · empty — UNBUILDABLE — buildLayersFromEngine always emits a root row' is truly unreachable, while 'Layers · list-view — UNBUILDABLE — no list-view exists' is simply not built.
evidence: Census of all 905 board names on 1:3, grouped by marker: RETIRED 16, design-ahead 23, not-implemented 9, UNBUILDABLE 7.
edit: Normalise to three prefixes, PRESERVING each board's existing evidence clause verbatim (several already carry file:line, which is better than any replacement I would write): [not-implemented] no producer, could be built · [unreachable] cannot happen by construction · RETIRED superseded by another board. Apply with scripts/figma/apply-truth-marks.mjs, which reads every rename back from the file before reporting. Hold until the module lanes report so a rename does not race a proposal on the same board.

claim: FIG-I-01 filed a blocker: two competing 'Tree row' masters, and four Layers findings waiting on which one wins. Its recommendation was to keep 2142:11082 — the shared-chrome set with a Depth 0-5 axis and 387 instances — and port 243:6's five parts into it.
truth: There is no competition to adjudicate, and the recommendation rests on a false premise. Measured across page 1:3: 2142:11082 has 387 instances in Journeys (225), Shell (117), Templates (27), Reference (9) and Components (9) — and ZERO in Layers. 243:6 has 57 instances and every one of them is a Layers board. evidence: Walked every INSTANCE on 1:3 resolving getMainComponentAsync to its COMPONENT_SET; counts above. 2142:11082 is a COMPONENT_SET of 12 variants (Depth 0-5 × State rest/selected) whose first variant contains a single TEXT 'body'. 243:6 is a COMPONENT with 7 children starting 'tint-bg'.
edit: Both renamed so the collision cannot recur, and the Library section corrected — its name called 2142:11082 'the set every editor board instances', which is true of a list row and false of the Layers row. The four Layers findings are unblocked and target 243:6. What 243:6 genuinely lacks is a depth axis, while the product indents at 12 + depth×16 (LayerTreeItem.tsx) — that, not a merge, is the real gap.

claim: The closing verification pass — a render check of every changed board, a type/colour conformance sweep, and the 110 boards the lanes never opened — was dispatched and had to stop partway.
truth: The account's Figma MCP quota is a RATE WINDOW, not a hard cap. It reported "You've reached the Figma MCP tool call limit for your Full seat on the Professional plan" and every call failed — then a single probe minutes later returned normally. I filed it as a hard cap first and that was wrong in the direction that mattered: it would have written off three verification passes as impossible when they were merely expensive.
evidence: Exhausted by a seven-node inspection loop — one call per node, the worst possible shape. Recovered on a single probe with no intervention. The three verification agents were told to stop, then corrected and told to resume with pacing rules: aggregate inside the sandbox and return counts rather than node lists, batch several boards per call, never one call per node.
edit: No Figma action. The lesson is a method one and belongs with the tooling: a read shape that costs one call per node cannot survey a 927-board file, and every sweep in scripts/figma/ that does the walk INSIDE one use_figma call is why the rest of this arc fitted in the budget. A null result from an exhausted window is indistinguishable from a null result on a clean board, which is the confusion this arc has been fighting all day — so the probe, not the retry, is the right response to a limit error.

claim: The OVERPRINT detector found 8 text pairs whose boxes intersect, and a fixer narrowed the 'title' of each to the gap before its 'meta'.
truth: The heuristic — leftmost node is the title, rightmost is the meta — is right for a real title/meta ROW and wrong for two nodes that start at nearly the same x. There the gap is negative, the width clamped to a 40px floor, and a 248x48 paragraph became 40x256. It did that to three nodes, RECREATING the SQUEEZED class the same sweep had just cleared. Four of the seven were genuine rows and are correctly fixed; three were not rows at all.
evidence: Read back after the run: 164:65 40x256, 303:2072 and 303:2088 both 40x120, and the next sweep reported them as SQUEEZED and TEXTOVER. Geometry afterwards showed the real shape — 164:65 'This colour comes from your brand tokens' at (16,32) 248x48 with 'Open Brand' at (16,76): the paragraph wrapped to two lines and collided with the button row BELOW it. Vertical, not horizontal.
edit: All three restored to their original widths, then fixed vertically: the lower elements pushed past the paragraph's real bottom and the parent frame grown. The fixer now REFUSES rather than guesses — a repair that would take a node below 60% of its width or below 80px is reported for human eyes instead of applied.

claim: Five geometric detectors were in place — OUT, TEXTOVER, SQUEEZED, OVERPRINT, ESCAPES — and the sweep reported the file clean on four of them.
truth: A whole class was still invisible, and it is the one that does the most damage: a node INSERTED into a fixed-height panel whose spacer below was never shrunk. Everything downstream then overprints its neighbour or falls off the bottom. `Media · no-results` lost its ENTIRE footer — the Upload / Browse stock row sits at y827 inside an 812-tall board — and nothing reported it, because no child is out of ITS parent and no two text nodes intersect.
evidence: Found by eye by the lot-B visual pass, which also identified the mechanisable assertion: for a fixed-height panel, the last child's bottom must equal the panel height. On 145:250 the OVERPRINT the sweep did report was only a SYMPTOM — the cause was a spacer 28px too tall.
fix: check-panel-stacks.mjs asserts it across every 812-tall panel, skipping parked hotspots. This class silently DELETES a UI region from a spec: a reviewer sees a panel with no footer and cannot tell whether the product has one.

target: the Card / media component — 50 instances across 13 boards
claim: The clipped STOCK pill was filed as four defects on four Media boards.
truth: It is ONE component bug seen four times. The Card / media component has 50 instances across 13 boards, and every one that shows the hero-dark card carries the clipped pill. A single component fix retires all of them.
fix: Auto-width the pill with 6px horizontal padding, or widen the fixed pill to 48px — once, in the component. And the methodological half, which is worth more: a targeted clip-risk query over 116 boards returned 9 candidates and ALL were benign. Clipping does not correlate with tight geometry, because a clipped label's own measured width IS the clipped width — the node reports as fitting. No geometric test can see this class, so it is the one place where eyes are the only instrument.

claim: The conformance harness records seven of the ten Client sign-off boards as verified: 'match'. A reader of that file would conclude the family is the best-verified in the section.

The one agent that opened all ten and screenshotted all ten can name a defect on every one of the seven — including an A0 identify board that draws NO FORM AT ALL, a form-shaped void between the paragraph and the button. All 10 sign-off rows have recipe: null. Independently, COVER-2 opened 10 of 10 and screenshotted 10 of 10.

Recorded because it is the same shape as the failure the repo has already paid for twice: a gate that reports a number nobody keyed, and a 'verified' field that outranks the thing it claims to have verified. The founder's own rule covers it — a null result is your harness until proven otherwise, and here the harness asserted a positive.

claim: A visual pass found one colour swatch (807:8367) rendering blue beside its label #1A1A1A. The conformance sweep had counted four #1A57DB paints — one digit off the accent — without knowing what any were for. I split them by role: one swatch, the rest ordinary accent use.
truth: The split was wrong and my fix shipped the error. ALL THREE are swatches. I checked only 807:8367 against its neighbouring label and classified the other two from it. 807:8586 captions #1A56DB, so accent blue was accidentally right. 807:8636 captions #E2E5F8 — a pale blue — and I painted it accent AND bound it to color/accent, so the chip contradicted its own caption and would have followed the accent forever after. That is the exact defect the visual pass reported, reintroduced one row down by the fix for it.
evidence: Read all three against their sibling labels after the fact: 807:8367 #1a1a1a beside '#1A1A1A' correct; 807:8586 #1a56db beside '#1A56DB' correct; 807:8636 #1a56db beside '#E2E5F8' WRONG. Found only because the check was finally run on all three rather than on the one that had been reported.
edit: 807:8636 restored to #E2E5F8, unbound. The rule is now stated in the script so it is not re-derived: a swatch equals the value it captions and is NEVER token-bound — check every candidate against its own label, never classify one from its neighbour.

target: 807:6965 — S1.2d - Conflict - Review both (Compare opens with conflict context)
claim: The last defect standing after the seven-detector sweep, reported as OVERPRINT: the bar title 'Resolve conflict' (x16 w107, ends 123) runs 23px into the mode strip at x100. Eight sibling Compare boards title the bar 'Compare' (w62, ends 78) against the same x100 strip, a 22px gutter, so the repair looked like a 22px nudge.
truth: It is not a geometry defect. Compare cannot enter a conflict state. ApprovedCompareView.tsx:146-183 renders no title (mode strip, spacer, count, page Select, refresh) and the header one level up, ReviewTab.tsx:500-504, is an unconditional literal reading "Compare with approved" — so no code path produces "Resolve conflict"; the whole version-history panel contains 'conflict' zero times; 'Review both' appears in no file in packages/editor or packages/dashboard; the only conflict code in the engine is OTEngine, reached only by CollaborationManager and HistoryManager, surfaced by no UI, behind NEXT_PUBLIC_FEATURE_COLLAB which CLAUDE.md marks demo-only and never on in production. The board draws a conflict title, a conflict count and a 'Conflict actions' row for a flow with no producer.
evidence: ApprovedCompareView.tsx:146-183 (toolbar children, no title node); ReviewTab.tsx:500-504 (the real header: Back + literal "Compare with approved"); grep 'conflict' packages/editor/src/editor/panels/version-history/ -> 0; grep 'Review both' packages/editor/src packages/dashboard -> 0; OTEngine consumers = CollaborationManager.ts:26,79,493 and HistoryManager.ts:325 only; CLAUDE.md Editor feature flags table.
edit: Prefixed [not-implemented] with the reason. Also moved the mode strip to x145 so the heading is no longer sheared through the control — a board marked unbuildable still has to be readable, and the sweep would otherwise report it forever.

claim: I recorded that all nine Compare boards draw a bar title `ApprovedCompareView`'s toolbar has no slot for, and filed it as a nine-board finding.
truth: That was overreach, caught by reading one level up. Compare DOES have a title bar — ReviewTab.tsx:500-504 renders a separate Toolbar above the view, holding a Back button and a literal span reading "Compare with approved". So the boards are right that a header exists; they are wrong about what is in it. The real deltas, all still live: the copy is "Compare with approved", not "Compare"; the header's left control is a BACK button, which no board draws; every board draws a `✕` close that exists in neither toolbar (Back is the exit); and the boards order page-select before the count where ApprovedCompareView renders count then Select. The title span is an unconditional literal, so it never varies by state — which leaves 807:6965's "Resolve conflict" unproduced by any code path and its [not-implemented] mark standing.
evidence: ReviewTab.tsx:500-504 (Toolbar > Button 'Back' + span 'Compare with approved', no conditional); ApprovedCompareView.tsx:147-183 (mode buttons, ToolbarSpacer, COUNT span, Select, refresh — no title, no close); nine boards measured: title x16 then strip x100 w219, 'Home ▾'@380, count@470, '✕'@1052.
edit: None on the boards. The finding itself corrected — the first version would have sent a later pass hunting a title that exists.

target: scripts/figma/render-defects.mjs — the first trustworthy full sweep
claim: Earlier runs of this sweep reported 927 boards with one or two defects, and that number was quoted in the arc report as evidence the file was near-clean.
truth: 203 defects across all 29 sections. The old number was three instrument bugs cancelling: rate-limit prose counted as defect lines (inflating), a 12-row-per-section print cap while the total counted all (deflating anything grepped from the output), and no resumability so a throttled run reported 0 and exited clean. Two more classes were found by an independent review and fixed before this run: a failed CLIPPED measurement defaulted to 'fits', and OUT exempted top overflow as a scroll region when only bottom overflow can be one. Breakdown: CONTAINER 101, OVERPRINT 51, CLIPPED 14, TEXTOVER 11, OUT 11, ESCAPES 11, UNMEASURED 4.
evidence: Full sweep, detector v3, 29 of 29 sections, exit 0. The run reported MIXED AGE (26 sections cached) — the cache is keyed by detector version so all 29 were measured by the same logic, and no Figma write ran during the sweep window, so the count is effectively single-moment. A --fresh re-run would remove even that caveat.
edit: None to the file. The number replaces the retracted one everywhere it was quoted.

target: ReviewBar.tsx:108 vs ReviewTab.tsx:295 — the same handler, two callers, one fixed
claim: A UX lane reported that the review bar's Re-send ships a client link that does not work.
truth: Confirmed independently, and the shape is worse than a plain bug. AquibraStudio.tsx:401-421 is the shared resendReview handler, and its own comment documents this exact defect and its fix: submitReview mints a token ONLY when given an email, so a re-send without one carried token: null and 'the client had no link to open — while the button said Re-send for review'. The panel was fixed — ReviewTab.tsx:295 passes round?.invitedEmail. The bar was not — ReviewBar.tsx:108 still calls onResend() with no argument. Both are wired to the same handler at AquibraStudio.tsx:536 and :584. A documented fix landed on one of its two call sites.
evidence: ReviewBar.tsx:105-108; ReviewTab.tsx:289-295; AquibraStudio.tsx:401-421,536,584. Read directly, not taken from the lane report.
edit: None — this is production code and out of bounds for this arc. Recorded so the board work does not draw a re-send affordance that the product cannot honour from the bar.

target: usePages.ts:120 vs ExportEngine.ts:120-122 — one field, two opposite readings
claim: A UX lane reported that every page badged Draft is in fact published.
truth: Confirmed by reading both files. They read the SAME field, page.settings.visibility, and disagree on undefined. usePages.ts:120 does `status: (p.settings?.visibility as PageItem['status']) ?? 'draft'`, so an unset visibility renders the badge 'Draft' (statusLabel.ts:14 maps it). isPageLive at ExportEngine.ts:120-122 does `return v === undefined || v === 'live'`, so the same unset value publishes. A page the panel calls Draft is on the internet. Compounding it: PageStatus (types.ts) declares seven states — live, draft, hidden, password, scheduled, error, external — and the Advanced tab offers three, so there is no control that sets draft at all.
evidence: usePages.ts:118-120; utils/statusLabel.ts:14; ExportEngine.ts:115-122 (whose own comment says a count that does not match what ships 'is the same lie one layer up'); types.ts:9.
edit: None — production code, out of bounds. Recorded because the Figma boards draw a Draft badge, and a board that shows Draft over a page the product publishes teaches the wrong model.

claim: Page ORDER decides which page the site serves at /.
truth: Confirmed. `resolveHomePageId` is `(pages.find(p => p.isHome) ?? pages[0])?.id`. Nothing sets isHome except an explicit user action, so on any site where nobody set one, the homepage is whichever page sorts first — and drag-reordering the Pages list, or deleting the top page, silently changes what the site serves at its root. No screen says so.
evidence: ExportEngine.ts:145-147, read directly.
edit: None — production code. Recorded so the Pages boards do not draw reorder as a purely cosmetic affordance.

claim: A UX lane reported the Publish panel refuses to publish on every fresh load of an already-published site.
truth: Confirmed by reading all three files. justPublished = uiState === 'published' && changeCount === 0. On a fresh load jobId is null (useState(null)), so uiState falls through its ternary to `hydratedUrl ? 'published' : 'idle'` — and an already-published site HAS a hydrated URL, so uiState is 'published' with no job in flight. changeCount comes from the undo stack, which HistoryManager.ts:156-157 empties on every project load by design ('Reset the stack and capture the loaded state as the single baseline'). Both halves are therefore true the moment the editor opens, so PublishTab:549 and :602 hide both 'what would go out' sections and the CTA greys. The topbar, reading the save clock instead, offers 'Publish changes' at the same moment.
evidence: PublishTab.tsx:222,462,549,602; usePublishJob.ts:130,299-311; HistoryManager.ts:152-161. Read directly, not taken from the lane report.
edit: None — production code, out of bounds for this arc. Recorded because the Publish boards must not draw a 'Published' resting state that the product cannot leave.

target: the generated-page head — correcting how this arc has been describing it
claim: This arc recorded that cms.service.ts clones the template head so every generated page carries a duplicate <title> AND the template's canonical and og:title.
truth: Half right, and the wrong half was mine. The duplicate <title> and meta description are real (cms.service.ts:212-215 appends before </head> without removing the template's, and browsers take the FIRST, so the template's title wins). But canonical and og:url are NOT the template's: the editor's export runs with no baseUrl so it emits no canonical at all, and lib/publish-html.ts:88-97 then injects a correct per-path one. What actually leaks is <title>, og:title, og:description and twitter:* — the tab title and the entire social card. A blank collection SEO title also emits a literal empty <title></title>.
evidence: cms.service.ts:212-215; lib/publish-html.ts:88-97; SEOInjector.ts:133-171; lib/publish-files.ts:82-84; lib/publish-urls.ts:91-92.
edit: The SEO boards should show the social card as the leaked surface, not canonical. Recorded ahead of that pass.
